svg.aria-label: How to write મંદિર: 5 parts, મ, ં, દ, િ, ર, one after another
svg.title: Writing મંદિર
svg.desc: 5 parts written one after another: મ, ં, દ, િ, ર (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: મ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, મ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ં: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/10_kam.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the anusvara drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; દ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, દ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; િ: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/2_ki.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the i sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ર: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ર animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: મ: The teaching app animates મ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper left, curls down through the left body and compact inner turn, then exits right across the long shoulder. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the left entry, compact inner turn, long shoulder, tall right spine, and lower foot, but its printed turns are wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's left-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the body, turn, shoulder, spine, foot, and terminals differently. ં: In the template for કં, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ં is one pen-down run: a small closed loop that starts at its top and turns anticlockwise. The printed dot is solid, so the pen path circles inside it. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 156 of its 157 stored prototypes of the anusvara are one stroke, 72% of them anticlockwise. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. દ: The teaching app animates દ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper right, circles left and around the rounded upper body, narrows through the middle turn, then continues left and around the broad lower body before rising into the lower-right terminal without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded upper body, narrow middle turn, broad lower body, and right terminal, but its printed bowls are wider and its terminal more compact than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-body-to-middle-turn-to-lower-body order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the bodies, turn, terminal, and endpoints differently. િ: In the template for કિ, and in all 34 consonant rows, િ is one pen-down run that starts at the right tip of the top hook, arcs up and to the left over the top, comes down the left stem and ends in a small foot to the right. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: its most common form of the i sign is two strokes (41 of 75 prototypes, 55%), but among its one-stroke prototypes (22 of 75) half start on the right and end at the lower left, as here. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ર: The teaching app animates ર as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, circles clockwise around the rounded upper body, narrows through the middle, curls around the small middle loop, then descends diagonally into the lower-right tail without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded upper body, narrow middle, small loop, and descending tail, but its printed turns are wider and more angular and its tail broader than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-body-to-middle-loop-to-lower-tail order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the body, loop, tail, and terminals differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 parts, one after another
Part 2 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 4 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, મ animation, first and second SVG paths
Part 2: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294,
1_k/10_kam.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the anusvara drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
Part 3: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, દ animation, first SVG path
Part 4: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294,
1_k/2_ki.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the i sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
Part 5: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ર animation, first SVG path
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
